HOMONYM, gender IS the meaning: de golf = wave/gulf; het golf = the ball game. The 'sports' theme fixes the game reading, so it must be 'h'. Dutch sport names are neuter (het voetbal, het tennis, het hockey)

expected.why: het kalf -> de kalveren (irregular -eren plural); 'Kalven' comes from a -lf->-lven rule that does not apply here
for the lemma as it now stands: 'het fruit' is a mass noun and has no plural; 'Drakenfruiten' is not Dutch. If countability is required, the lemma must change (see singular HOLD)
two errors: het dossier -> de dossiers (not -en), and the attributive adjective must inflect in the plural. The script inflected only the last token
Van Dale: het slot -> de sloten (open-syllable lengthening), so hangslot -> hangsloten. 'Hangslotten' is the script's blind consonant-doubling rule; slot does NOT double (contrast pot -> potten)

the brief's own worked example, and it holds: themes=at_the_supermarket -> this is kitchen salt, a mass noun. 'Zouten' is the chemical/technical plural (classes of salts) and is flatly wrong for a supermarket picture shown to a 3-7 year old. metadata countable:true is the known-fallible hint

Weather phenomenon, not counted in child-facing Dutch ('het onweer'). Van Dale does record a rare plural 'onweren', so I do not call the current form a hard spelling error - but it is not a word to speak to a 3-7 year old; several thunderstorms are 'onweersbuien'. p = s per the file convention.
Van Dale: het pad -> de paden. 'Padden' is the plural of the ANIMAL 'de pad'; the script applied the toad's doubling rule to the footpath, so a child sees a trail and hears 'toads'.

'blad' has a long a, so consonant doubling is impossible - 'Driebladden' cannot be a Dutch word. Compounds in -blad take -bladen (tafelblad -> tafelbladen, dekblad -> dekbladen); 'bladeren' is reserved for leaves on a tree.
